projects.title: Clinical Decisions: The Nurse’s EHR Challenge
projects.subtitle: Can you spot what’s missing in a patient record before it becomes a safety risk?
projects.description: A scenario-based EHR simulation where nurses practice accurate, safe and policy-aligned documentation inside a realistic (fictional) hospital record system at Rivermere Health.
projects.overview: Learners step into Rivermere Health, a fictional hospital, and work through a mock electronic health record. Guided by Evelyn, their head nurse, they select the right patient and encounter, review a nursing note for documentation gaps, and choose the safest next action. The experience takes 10–15 minutes and lets learners retry.
projects.problem: Documentation errors in EHRs, like choosing the wrong patient among look-alike records or leaving gaps in a nursing note, are a patient-safety risk. Policy documents explain the rules, but nurses rarely get to practice applying them in a system that looks and behaves like the real thing.
projects.solution: I built a realistic EHR interface (patient search, banner, tabs for notes, vitals, medications and orders) and wrapped it in two branching scenarios: (1) select the correct patient and encounter from near-duplicate records using two identifiers, and (2) find the gaps in a pain-assessment note and choose the appropriate next action. Each step has narrated audio, a progress tracker, on-demand help and job-aid style feedback checklists.
projects.results: Learners practice three high-stakes skills in a risk-free environment: patient identification, record review, and escalation decisions, with feedback tied directly to documentation policy.
process: Identified the target behaviors: verify two patient identifiers, review records for completeness, escalate safely
Wrote the realistic scenarios and distractors (near-duplicate patients, incomplete pain documentation)
Designed the mock EHR interface and the Rivermere Health brand
Storyboarded the slides, help screens and pause menus
Added narration, a progress tracker and retry paths
Built the interactive simulation in Articulate Storyline

documents.title: Performance Problem Analysis
documents.intro: Self-initiated portfolio project based on a hypothetical healthcare organization. This document frames a potential workplace performance problem before a training solution is selected.

blocks.heading: Context
blocks.text: Rivermere Health is a fictional healthcare organization that provides inpatient care. Newly hired nurses must use an electronic health record (EHR) system to document patient assessments, enter clinical information, and review records. The organization wants to investigate whether onboarding nurses experience difficulties completing accurate, complete, and consistent electronic documentation.

blocks.heading: Performance problem
blocks.text: The organization is concerned that newly hired nurses may enter incomplete or inconsistent information, select inappropriate documentation fields, or fail to identify errors when reviewing electronic patient records. This is a hypothetical problem statement to guide investigation; it has not been validated using actual employee performance data or interviews.

blocks.heading: Desired performance
blocks.text: Nurses should select the correct patient and encounter, accurately document the supplied clinical information in the appropriate fields, complete required documentation, identify inconsistencies, and follow the organization's approved review and record-completion procedures.

blocks.heading: Potential gap to investigate
blocks.text: Current performance is not yet known. The potential gap is the difference between the expected EHR documentation workflow and nurses' actual performance in realistic documentation situations.

blocks.heading: Possible contributing factors
text: Knowledge or skill: Nurses may not understand documentation requirements or may lack practice navigating the EHR.
Process clarity: Documentation procedures may be unclear or difficult to locate.
Tools or access: Nurses may have insufficient access to practice environments or usable guidance.
Work environment: Time pressure, interruptions, or competing demands may contribute to documentation errors.
Reinforcement: Supervisors may not consistently provide feedback or reinforce approved documentation practices.

blocks.heading: Questions to investigate
text: What documentation errors, omissions, or near misses have been observed, and how frequently do they occur?
What does the organization's documentation policy require nurses to do?
Can nurses locate the correct patient, enter information accurately, and review records in a realistic practice environment?
Are the EHR interface, onboarding materials, and documentation procedures clear and accessible?
Do nurses need training, guided practice, job aids, workflow improvements, or a combination of interventions?
How will the organization measure whether documentation performance improves?

blocks.heading: ID recommendation
blocks.text: Do not assume that training alone will solve the problem. First validate the performance gap and investigate its causes. If nurses lack the knowledge or skills needed to document accurately, a short scenario-based EHR simulation may help them practise patient selection, data entry, error identification, and record review. If the main barriers involve unclear procedures, interface design, workload, or limited access to practice, those issues should also be addressed.

documents.title: Needs Analysis
documents.intro: Define the intended learners, their current capability, the desired performance, relevant constraints, and the information to obtain from subject-matter experts (SMEs) before deciding what instruction to build.

blocks.heading: Learners
blocks.text: Newly hired registered nurses or nurses transitioning into a hospital that uses an electronic health record (EHR). Adult professionals with varied levels of EHR experience, digital confidence, prior clinical settings, and familiarity with local documentation policies.

blocks.heading: Current capability
blocks.text: They may understand basic nursing documentation principles and the importance of accurate patient records from prior education or clinical practice. They may be uncertain about navigating the specific EHR, choosing the correct patient or encounter, entering information into the appropriate fields, recognizing missing or inconsistent information, or following the local review and completion process.

blocks.heading: Desired performance
blocks.text: Given a fictional patient scenario and the organization’s approved rules, the nurse completes the selected documentation workflow accurately and consistently: select the correct patient and encounter; place supplied information in the appropriate fields; identify missing or inconsistent details; review the record before completion; and choose the appropriate next action when an issue is identified.

blocks.heading: Tools
blocks.text: Developed in Articulate Storyline 360 with a polished, modern hospital interface, restrained animation, clear navigation, immediate feedback, and retry functionality.

blocks.heading: Information needed from subject-matter experts
text: Which documentation task should be taught? What information is required, where does it belong, what terminology is approved, and what makes an entry complete and accurate?

What are the exact steps? Which errors or omissions matter most? What should a nurse do when information is missing, contradictory, or entered in the wrong place? What actions must never be simulated as acceptable?

What do new nurses struggle with most? What evidence supports this (observations, de-identified audits, incident trends, educator feedback, or competency checks)? What can learners already do independently?
Which current policies and procedures govern the task? Are there organization-specific rules, escalation steps, or legal requirements that the simulation must reflect?

What would count as competent performance? Which critical errors should trigger corrective feedback? What score or completion standard is appropriate, and who will review and approve the final scenario?

documents.note: This is a fictional, self-initiated instructional design portfolio project. Rivermere Health, the learner scenario, and the potential performance issues are hypothetical and are not based on data from a real healthcare organization. The questions and suggested information to obtain from subject-matter experts were drafted with assistance from OpenAI’s ChatGPT; they are proposed prompts, not findings supplied or validated by actual subject-matter experts. Before any real-world use, clinical details, documentation requirements, and policies must be verified with qualified healthcare subject-matter experts and authoritative organizational sources.

2. Review the available chart information.
Skipping relevant information or overlooking a mismatch in the supplied details.
Explore clearly labeled chart panels and identify information relevant to the task.
3. Review information in the appropriate documentation fields.
Placing supplied information in the wrong field or treating an incomplete note as complete.
Inspect a sample note containing predefined, reviewable issues.
4. Identify missing or inconsistent details.
Overlooking a predefined omission or guessing an unsupported detail.
Select issues supported by the fictional record and the rules shown in the simulation.
5. Choose the appropriate next action.
Ignoring a discrepancy, guessing missing information, or proceeding without following the stated procedure.
Choose among scenario options, receive explanatory feedback, and retry during practice.
